text.p: The following are the main stories in Slovenia's Friday morning newspapers.

- Slovenia was ordered to pay the costs of a Cyprus court case regarding the money of the former Yugoslavia deposited in the Cypriot branch of Yugoslav Beogradska banka although the country does not see the case as resolved.
- According to Slovenian legislation presidential elections have to be held by November 16 this year.
- Heavy rain caused 73 million tolars of damage ($0.4 million) in the city of Trbovlje, east of Ljubljana on Tuesday.
- Construction of a new electricity plant to the value of 3.7 million marks in Tolmin, north-west of Ljubljana, will be the highest investment in the area around Tolmin this year.
- The number of guests in Slovenia's health resorts in the first six mounths this year increased by six percent compared to the same period of 1996.
- The Maribor general hospital posted a loss of 94 miilion tolars in the first half of this year due to higher spending on medical equipment.

- The state prosecutor accused the chief executive of SCT, one of the largest constuction companies in Slovenia, of breaching his authority by enabling irregular partial privatisation of the company in 1990.

- In the past three years Slovenia earned 28 billion tolars in cash from the sell-off of over 1,000 companies in a massive privatisation drive, while the remaining equity was purchased by privatisation vouchers distributed to all citizens.
- According to rumours Slovenian car trader Autocommerce plans to buy tourist company Kompas Turizem later this year.
- The management board of trader Mercator is expected to present the future stategy of the company to the firm's supervisory board on Monday.
